scope: Compare the installed GTK2 down-stepper glyph in normal, pressed and released states against the stored native SR10.4/VUE measured rows and palette.

method.reference_scope: Measured 11x11 native down-arrow glyph rows and role colors from Domain/OS SR10.4 + HP VUE 2.01; comparison uses the stored pixel-row encoding, not a retained full held screenshot.
method.comparison: RGB/RGBA equality for 71 glyph pixels at asset offset (2,2), ignoring the outer widget cell and cursor-overlap/context symbols. No scale or interpolation.

asset_integrity.palette_provenance: R509 documents palette-generated GTK2 assets and semantic KDE roles; no source RGB was changed.

live_vm_session.profile: paused=false, frameskip=4, throttled=false, mouse button released
live_vm_session.after_counter_probe: A one-count (+1,+1) relative probe completed and auto-cleared its axes. The immediately captured guest screen was black; one documented one-frame Shift pulse restored VUE. The follow-up capture shows the same windows and cursor location. No click or scrollbar hold was sent.

result: The existing installed GTK2 down-arrow artwork matches all 71 encoded native glyph pixels in normal, held and released states at 1:1. The held asset exchanges the same 53 light/shadow bevel pixels as the measured VUE state; release uses the exact normal asset. No asset or GTK2 configuration change is indicated for this down glyph.
limits: This compares the glyph only, not the full 15x15 GTK2 widget cell or a live GTK2 hold capture.
The reference was retained as measured rows and colors, not a raw held-state screenshot in this evidence set.
The VM input attempt did not produce a held scrollbar state; no claim is made about horizontal/up arrow historical held rendering, content scrolling, hover or disabled states.
This is the DomainOS color scheme only; semantic roles and palette regeneration remain required for other schemes.
next: Keep GTK2/I167 active. Preserve the verified down-arrow asset. Continue only if a remaining mismatch is reproduced; keep unmeasured states as explicit limits and do not infer their historical appearance from the down-arrow glyph.
